title: omarchy-m-test report, schema version 1
description: The report the omarchy-m-test CLI produces and the site's /api/v1 upload accepts. Shared by cli/ and site/; golden reports in schema/golden/ must validate against it. Only allowlisted, privacy-safe fields are permitted, so every object rejects unknown properties.

schema_version.description: Report schema version. Bumped on any incompatible change.

consent_version.description: Version of the disclaimer the user accepted.

catalogue_version.description: Version of the feature catalogue (catalogue/catalogue.json) the results were classified with.

machine.description: What the Mac is. Model and chip come from the device tree, never from serial numbers or other per-unit identifiers.

model.description: Device-tree model string, e.g. "Apple MacBook Pro (16-inch, M2 Max, 2023)".

board.description: Board id from the device-tree compatible list, e.g. "j416c".

soc.description: SoC id from the device-tree compatible list, e.g. "t6021".

chip.description: Marketing chip name for the SoC, e.g. "M2 Max" or "A18 Pro"; "unknown" when the SoC isn't known yet.

system.description: What the Mac runs: package names and versions, the os-release ID and the kinds of block devices under the root filesystem; never device names, UUIDs or key slots.

stack.description: converged (the omarchy-mac or omarchy package), mx-mac (the fork's omarchy-dev without omarchy-mac), legacy-omarchy-mac (no Omarchy package, but omarchy-mac-keyring or a checkout), or reference for another distro.

distro.description: os-release ID, e.g. "omarchy" or "fedora"; "unknown" without one.

encryption.description: Whether the root filesystem is on an encrypted volume.

candidate_set.description: The candidate set a candidate image was built from: the candidate_set of the image's target record (image/target or, after first boot, image/target.booted), else of the factory seal. Absent without a target record.

image.description: The image's own build record: these keys of its target record (/var/lib/omarchy/image/target, or image/target.booted after the first boot), as the image builder writes them. Absent without a target record; older images have only format and platform.

platform.description: The platform the image was built for, e.g. apple-silicon.

candidate_set.description: The candidate set the image was built from.

candidate_source_commit.description: The omarchy-mac commit the candidate set was built from.

builder_tree_clean.description: Whether the builder's tree was clean.

package_set_sha256.description: The digest of the image's installed package set, as its release's IMAGE and PROVENANCE give it; with built, it names the release asset.

built.description: When the image was built, UTC.

packages.description: Installed versions of the stack, boot and hardware packages omarchy-m-test asks pacman about.

unattended.description: Present (true) when nobody was at the Mac for the run (omarchy-m-test --unattended): only the automatic checks ran, every human check is skipped with that reason, and nothing disruptive was done. Absent when someone was there to be asked.

inventory.description: The hardware inventory: for each kind of device-tree node the Mac has, its status and whether a driver claimed it; the enabled nodes no driver claimed, explained against the catalogue; and the running kernel's build options compared with Asahi's. Only node types (the first compatible string), statuses, driver-bound states, counts and build-option names and values: never a property value or a node's path. Absent when the Hardware section wasn't run.

nodes.description: Hardware nodes grouped by type, status and driver state.

compatible.description: The node's first compatible string, e.g. "apple,t6020-avd".

driver.description: bound: a driver claimed the node's device; unbound: it has a device no driver claimed; none: no device of its own (disabled, set up early by the kernel core, or handled by its parent's driver).

unclaimed.description: Enabled nodes with a device no driver claimed, by type. outcome is unknown-hardware when the catalogue's hardware map doesn't know the node; otherwise the node counts as its feature failing, classified like a check.

feature.description: Catalogue feature id, when the catalogue knows the hardware.

deferred.description: Why the kernel says the device is still waiting for its driver (debugfs devices_deferred; needs root), with node paths cut to the node's name.

kernel_config.description: The running kernel's build options (/proc/config.gz) against Asahi's reference configuration. Only options set to y, m, n (not set) or a number are compared; toolchain-derived options are left out.

id.description: Check id. The known ids are the catalogue's checks; the site rejects ids it doesn't know.

answered_by_default.description: A human check answered yes by a bare Enter (the prompt's default) rather than a typed y: it passes, but the site shows it as unconfirmed and never counts it towards a feature's state. Absent when the answer was typed, and on automatic checks.

score.description: A benchmark's measurement (benchmark.* checks that passed): the value in its unit (points for glmark2 and vkmark, frames per second for decode), the tool and version that measured it, and the benchmark suite: the version of omarchy-m-test's fixed scenes, clip and settings. Only scores of the same check, suite and unit are compared. Absent on every other check.

value.description: A whole number: reports carry no floating-point numbers (the signature's canonical form).

classification.description: The result explained against the feature catalogue: Aurora's expected state first, then Asahi's.

expected.description: Each layer's expected state for this Mac, from the catalogue. Empty when the catalogue doesn't cover the chip.

signature.description: The machine key's signature, which the site requires. The CLI creates an ed25519 key on the Mac's first run and signs every report with it (ssh-keygen -Y sign, namespace omarchy-m-test-report) over the report's canonical form: the report without this member, as JSON with keys sorted, no whitespace and non-ASCII characters as UTF-8. The site verifies it and groups reports by a keyed digest of the public key; neither the key nor the signature is shown or exported.

public_key.description: The OpenSSH public key, without a comment.

signature.description: The armored SSH signature, as ssh-keygen -Y sign prints it.
